text:
Alex (acct-exec): FYI — MercuryFunds wants to run a week-long PrivateDeploy POC. Their net team asks: TGW/peering vs PrivateLink tradeoffs for sustained ~200 Mbps, can Redwood preserve client src IP if traffic goes via their TLS-inspecting appliance, and exact firewall rules/ports we need them to open? Also they asked about DNS when using PrivateLink.

Diego (network): Quick summary: TGW/peering = L3 connectivity so client src IP preserved. PrivateLink = interface endpoints in their subnets; traffic terminates on our ENIs so the src IP seen by the service is the ENI IP unless the proxy forwards client IP in headers. For TLS-inspect proxies, if they terminate TLS then SNI may not be visible to the backend.

Priya (solutions): For 200 Mbps sustained, TGW or direct VPC peering is typically lower cost (no per-GB interface endpoint fees). PrivateLink has per-hour + per-GB charges on most clouds and is great for minimizing network footprint and for customers that don't want to deal with route tables. Recommend TGW if they care about cost and src IP.

Nina (security): Compliance note: MercuryFunds needs end-to-end audit logs with original client IP for investigations. If they insist on TLS inspection, ask them to configure the appliance to inject X-Forwarded-For and to rotate certs with a key exchange plan. We can also produce a signed header (X-Redwood-Client) to assert request provenance.

Tom (runtime): We can add headers: X-Forwarded-For and X-Redwood-Signed. Example header format we will send when present: ```
X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.37
X-Redwood-Signed: v1:eyJhbGciOi...
```
If the proxy strips headers or performs MITM without forwarding, original IP cannot be reconstructed.

Diego (network): Firewall checklist (customer side) — substitute their CIDRs and our provided ENI ranges: ```
# allow outbound from customer internet/proxy to our service
allow tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to 100.65.200.0/24 port 443 # PrivateLink ENIs
allow tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to 10.30.0.0/16 port 443 # TGW/peering internal routes
allow udp/tcp 53 to their DNS resolver for name resolution
# ephemeral callbacks (if using streaming or callbacks)
allow tcp from 100.65.200.0/24 to 10.20.0.0/16 ports 1024-65535
```
Also allow outbound to our healthcheck IPs.

Alex (acct-exec): They want a single CIDR to paste into their firewall ticket. Diego — can infra-bot reserve a placeholder block for the POC?

infra-bot: POC environment provisioned: redwood-poc-mercury-2025. Placeholder ENI CIDR: 100.65.200.0/24. Update will be posted after allocation.

Priya (solutions): DNS notes: with PrivateLink AWS supports private DNS names that resolve to the ENI IPs if they enable the interface endpoint DNS. If they keep their own resolver or use DoH/DoT at the proxy, ensure DNS queries to internal resolvers are allowed. If they override DNS, make sure our service FQDN resolves to the ENI IPs.

Nina (security): If they use TLS inspection, we should agree on: 1) header attestation method, 2) key rotation cadence, 3) least privilege for log access. I'll send a 6-question security mini-FAQ for signature.

Tom (runtime): Action item: we'll run a quick test harness that simulates TLS-inspect proxy and a NAT path to verify header preservation and streaming behavior. Assigning to Jordan. ETA 24 hours.

Alex (acct-exec): Great — I'll send the checklist + placeholder CIDR to MercuryFunds' firewall and loop in their proxy engineer. Send any wording changes to me before I hit send.

Diego (network): One more tip for them: if they want to preserve original client source port for forensic correlation, use TGW/peering. PrivateLink will collapse source to the ENI.

Alex (acct-exec): Thanks team :raised_hands:
